name: Indian trajectory and calibration datasets (Chennai Saidapet / ETF2D, NCR UAV, SkyEye Ahmedabad, two-wheeler seepage benchmark, IDS-JODHA, IIT Guwahati highway data)

first_release: Chennai Saidapet 2014-2015 (recorded 13 Feb 2014; data legend dated 14 Oct 2014; TRR 2491, 2015). SkyEye 2019 (arXiv 1912.04801). ETF2D report 2025. IDS-JODHA October 2025. NCR UAV December 2025 (arXiv 2512.11898). Seepage benchmark 11 July 2026. IIT Guwahati UAV paper 2026.
last_activity: Seepage benchmark v1 published 11 July 2026. NCR UAV Zenodo record (sample clips) created 18 May 2026. IIT Guwahati paper 2026 (DOI 10.1007/s13177-026-00657-2). Chennai Technion files unchanged since 2014.
licence: Chennai Saidapet: no licence stated; the legend asks users to cite Kanagaraj et al. (2015) [uncertain]. ETF2D report: CC BY 4.0 (a report, not data). NCR UAV: CC BY 4.0 on the Zenodo record that the DOI resolves to (sample video clips); licence of trajectory files not confirmed [uncertain]. Seepage benchmark: CC BY-NC 4.0. IDS-JODHA: CC BY 4.0. SkyEye: not stated [uncertain]. IIT Guwahati highway data: no public release found [uncertain].
language: N/A (data files: XLSX, CSV, MP4, ZIP, rosbag)
code_availability: Chennai Saidapet: public XLSX files at toledo.net.technion.ac.il. NCR UAV: Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.17745347. Seepage: Mendeley Data DOI 10.17632/hs6drgb2vx.1. IDS-JODHA: Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.17258045, plus a project page with codes. SkyEye: the pointer at github.com/debadityaroy/SkyEye returned HTTP 404 on 2026-11-11. ETF2D: report PDF only (DOI 10.25368/2025.122). IIT Guwahati: paper only.
maintenance_health: All of these are static research releases with no maintenance cadence. The Chennai files have stayed online since 2014 and are the de facto Indian benchmark, reused by Kulkarni et al. 2024 and the ETF2D project. SkyEye's link has rotted. The NCR Zenodo DOI now resolves to a version holding only sample video clips, so whether the trajectory files are still reachable must be checked by hand [uncertain].
mixed_traffic_support: Chennai Saidapet: 6 classes (motorcycle, car, bus, truck, LCV, auto-rickshaw); composition 56.4% motorcycles, 26.6% cars, 12.2% autos, 4.8% heavy vehicles; each record carries vehicle length and width. NCR UAV: 6 classes (car, motorised two-wheeler, motorised three-wheeler, LCV, bus, HCV), with car:M2W:M3W:LCV:Bus:HCV shares of about 35-41 : 31-45 : 10-15 : 4-11 : 1-2 : 1-6 percent across sites. SkyEye: lane-less intersection traffic, all road users tracked. Seepage benchmark: two-wheeler seepage events from Indian videos (IDD/TIAND).
non_lane_behaviour: Chennai Saidapet records continuous lateral position (centre of vehicle, measured from the left edge), lateral speed and lateral acceleration for every vehicle at 0.5 s, so lateral placement and lateral gaps can be measured directly. NCR UAV gives X,Y local coordinates at 30 fps; the paper reports lane-keeping preferences and wide lateral distributions for two-wheelers. ETF2D and Kulkarni et al. (2024) used the Chennai data to define leader-follower pairs through lateral overlap and influence zones.
seepage_filtering_support: Only the Mendeley seepage benchmark (hs6drgb2vx) targets seepage directly. It holds processed detections, extracted seepage-event annotations and simulation calibration outputs; the raw IDD and TIAND videos are not included and must be obtained from idd.insaan.iiit.ac.in. Which simulator it calibrated, and the file sizes and formats, are not stated on the landing page [uncertain]. Chennai and NCR are midblock sets and show filtering only indirectly.
per_class_parameters: Chennai Saidapet (Kanagaraj et al. 2015): mean instantaneous speed is 6.13 m/s for cars, 6.01 for motorcycles, 5.64 for heavy vehicles, 5.06 for autos and 5.88 overall, with a range of 0-15.22 m/s; total flow is 6,010 veh/h in one direction on a 3-lane, 11.2 m carriageway. NCR UAV: lowest mean speed 11.22 km/h at DEL_3; other sites have speed distributions centred near 30-35 km/h. Beyond Lanes (UAV urban arterial, IIT Kanpur and TU Dresden, arXiv 2608.00602): median two-wheeler length 2.01 m and width 0.73 m; autos about 2.92 m x 1.35 m; cars mean width 1.85 m (SD 0.12) [uncertain class mapping]. IIT Guwahati Delhi 8-lane highway: jam density about 900 veh/km across the full road width.
indian_calibration_evidence: Chennai data used for: leader-follower identification and Wiedemann-99 calibration (Kulkarni, Chaudhari et al. 2024; holdout of 187 pairs from a 70/30 split; best method gives position RMSE of about 6.9-7.1 m [uncertain exact value]); IDM driver-heterogeneity analysis and the Intelligent-Agent Model in ETF2D; continuum and areal fundamental diagrams (arXiv 2408.02353, Chennai/Surat/Guwahati). NCR UAV: validated against classified volume counts, class space-mean speeds and a probe-vehicle trajectory. IIT Guwahati highway: the Underwood speed-density model fit best among six classical models and two ML models.
calibration_dataset_used: CHENNAI SAIDAPET (= the Chennai data in ETF2D). Six-lane divided urban arterial on the Maraimalai Adigalar Bridge, Saidapet, Chennai, northbound; section 245 m long and 11.2 m wide; on a bridge, so no junctions, bus stops or parking; 13 Feb 2014, 14:45-15:15; 3,005 trajectories, 111,629 observations at 0.5 s; open. DOI 10.25368/2025.122 (ETF2D) is the DFG final report of the TU Dresden project, not a dataset; its Chennai analysis uses the Kanagaraj et al. (2015) data, according to Kulkarni et al. (2024). ETF2D's own new dataset, MiTra, is from Milan, Italy (DOI 10.25532/OPARA-881), not India. NCR UAV: six midblock sites, Delhi DEL_2 to DEL_5 and Noida NDA_1 and NDA_2, each 41-66 min, stretches of 170-200 m, widths of 10.5-14 m [uncertain per-row mapping], 30 fps. SKYEYE: four intersections in Ahmedabad, about 1 hour of aerial footage each, with tracks and safe/unsafe interaction labels. IDS-JODHA: dashcam (4K, 25 fps, about 88,700 frames) plus VLP-16 LiDAR (about 16,800 scans), about 59 min in Jodhpur; no trajectory annotations stated. IIT GUWAHATI: drone video on an 8-lane divided highway on the outskirts of Delhi, more than 36,000 vehicles, 10 fps, 8,938,920 data points; no public download found. Separately, arXiv 2408.02353 used a Guwahati state-highway section that has not been released.
calibration_method: N/A for datasets; see indian_calibration_evidence for the methods studies applied to them (RMSE of position for leader-follower calibration; speed-density model fitting).
max_density_tested: IIT Guwahati: jam density about 900 veh/km across the 8-lane road width. Chennai: medium flow with some stop-and-go; 6,010 veh/h over 11.2 m [uncertain peak density, not read]. NCR: from near free flow to heavy congestion (DEL_3 mean 11.22 km/h).
validation_against_field_case: Maraimalai Adigalar Bridge, Saidapet, Chennai (6-lane divided arterial). NCR midblocks in Delhi and Noida. Four Ahmedabad intersections (SkyEye). No dataset covers a named junction such as Silk Board or Hebbal.
demand_input_formats: Chennai: entry times and classes of the 3,005 vehicles can be replayed as an exact inflow schedule at the upstream end of the 245 m section. NCR: classified flows per site (composition given in Table 1 of the paper).
data_access: 1) CHENNAI SAIDAPET (Technion): https://toledo.net.technion.ac.il/files/2014/10/ChennaiTrajectoryData2.45-3.00PM.xlsx (7,087,561 bytes, checked 2026-11-11) and https://toledo.net.technion.ac.il/files/2014/10/ChennaiTrajectoryData3.00-3.15PM.xlsx (size not measured, likely similar), legend at https://toledo.net.technion.ac.il/files/2014/10/TrajectoryDataDescription.pdf; XLSX with 12 columns (vehicle number, type 1-6, time, length, width, longitudinal position, speed, acceleration, lateral position, speed, acceleration, overlap-correction flag); no registration; licence not stated, cite Kanagaraj et al. TRR 2491 (2015). 2) ETF2D (DOI 10.25368/2025.122): report PDF at https://tud.qucosa.de/api/qucosa%3A97638/attachment/ATT-0/ (CC BY 4.0), not a dataset. 3) NCR UAV (arXiv 2512.11898): paper says all trajectory datasets are at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.17745347, but on 2026-11-11 this resolved to a CC BY 4.0 record of sample MP4 clips (Del2 25.1 MB, Del4 22.9 MB, NDA 21.4 MB; 69.3 MB total); trajectory file format and size unconfirmed because Zenodo's API blocked automated access [uncertain]; fields per paper: vehicle ID, timestamp (30 fps), X,Y in metres, length, width, speed (km/h), longitudinal and lateral acceleration, class. 4) SKYEYE (arXiv 1912.04801): pointer https://github.com/debadityaroy/SkyEye returned 404 on 2026-11-11, so it is currently unobtainable without contacting the authors [uncertain]. 5) SEEPAGE BENCHMARK: https://data.mendeley.com/datasets/hs6drgb2vx/1 , CC BY-NC 4.0, file list and size not shown [uncertain]; raw videos from IDD/TIAND at idd.insaan.iiit.ac.in (registration likely required [uncertain]). 6) IDS-JODHA: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.17258045 , CC BY 4.0, 176.1 GB in three ZIPs (Monocular Rain Data 61.1 GB, Multi-Modal Dataset 115.0 GB, Metadata and Codes 14.9 kB). 7) IIT GUWAHATI highway: no download found; paper DOI 10.1007/s13177-026-00657-2; data availability not stated [uncertain].
reuse_mode: Use as data. MOST PRACTICAL IN 72 HOURS: the Chennai Saidapet set (Technion). It is the only one that is small (two XLSX files of about 7 MB each), directly downloadable without registration, already in physical units (metres, m/s, 0.5 s), includes lateral position and vehicle dimensions, and is the established benchmark. What each set can calibrate or validate: Chennai gives the speed-density/flow scatter from 1-min aggregates, per-class speed distributions, time and space headways, lateral position and lateral gap distributions, and IDM parameters per class; it has no junction discharge. NCR UAV gives the same quantities plus fundamental diagrams across 6 sites and two widths (10.5 m and 14 m), which is good for testing how capacity changes with width, if the trajectory files can be fetched. SkyEye would give intersection turning and conflict trajectories and junction discharge, but is not obtainable. The seepage benchmark gives the rate and conditions of two-wheeler seepage at queues, but needs the raw IDD/TIAND videos for full use and is non-commercial. IIT Guwahati gives a jam density reference (about 900 veh/km over 8 lanes) from the paper only. IDS-JODHA is a perception dataset (dashcam plus LiDAR, 176 GB) and is not useful for calibration within 72 hours.
effort_within_72_hours: Chennai validation, about 4-6 hours: (1) download the two XLSX files and convert them to CSV once offline; (2) build a 245 m x 11.2 m straight one-way link in the simulator; (3) inject the observed entry schedule (time, class, length, width, entry lateral position) at the upstream edge; (4) run, place virtual detectors every 50 m, and aggregate to 1-min flow, density and space-mean speed; (5) compare per-class mean speeds against the observed 6.13 / 6.01 / 5.64 / 5.06 m/s (cars / motorcycles / heavy / autos), the lateral-position histograms by class, and the speed-density cloud. Report the error per class (e.g. mean absolute percentage error) and note that this is one 30-min sample. Cut: trajectory-level calibration with an optimiser, leader-follower identification, and every other dataset. Junction discharge cannot be validated from Chennai, so use the Indo-HCM saturation-flow formula (1140 - 60 W PCU/h/m) as the junction target instead.
licence_constraint: Chennai: no licence, so cite the paper and do not redistribute the files inside the app without permission; loading them at build time for a validation report is fine [uncertain]. Seepage benchmark CC BY-NC 4.0 bars commercial use. NCR and IDS-JODHA CC BY 4.0 require attribution only.
known_limitations: Chennai: one site, one 30-min afternoon period, medium flow, on a bridge with no side friction or junctions; trajectories were extracted semi-automatically at 0.5 s; 4,199 observations (3.73%) were manually corrected for overlaps and are flagged and should be excluded from microscopic analysis; the classes do not separate bicycles or pedestrians. NCR: midblock only; the DOI's current version shows only sample clips. SkyEye: unavailable. Seepage benchmark: derived from dashcam-style IDD/TIAND footage; raw video is not included; non-commercial. IDS-JODHA: no trajectory labels. IIT Guwahati: highway, not urban; data not released. None of the open sets covers a signalized junction with stop-line discharge measurements.
documented_failures: Several Indian trajectory sets announced as public later became unreachable (SkyEye GitHub 404; NCR concept DOI now pointing at sample clips). The ETF2D DOI given in the task is a project report, not a Chennai dataset, so it is easy to misidentify sources. Kanagaraj et al. note that most developing-world trajectory data are not public, which is why the 2014 Chennai set is still reused a decade later.
validation_approach: Chennai: locally weighted regression smoothing gives consistent position, speed and acceleration, with no trajectory overlaps after correction; ANOVA confirms class speed differences are significant (F(3,3001) = 114.93). NCR: compared against classified volume counts, class space-mean speeds and a probe-vehicle trajectory. Availability and sizes in this item were checked by HTTP download on 2026-11-11.
takeaway_for_our_build: Ship one honest empirical check: a Chennai Saidapet replay scenario (245 m x 11.2 m, observed entry schedule) that reports simulated against observed per-class mean speeds, lateral-position histograms and the 1-min speed-density cloud. Pair it with Indo-HCM saturation-flow and lane-capacity targets for junctions and width, because no open Indian dataset validates junction discharge. Label the result 'checked against one 30-min Chennai midblock sample', not 'calibrated for Indian traffic'. Store the converted CSV outside the app bundle and cite Kanagaraj et al. (2015).
